question: Which documents count as Officially Valid Documents (OVDs) for KYC of an individual?
answer:
"Officially Valid Document" (OVD) means the passport, the driving licence, proof of possession of Aadhaar number, the Voter's Identity Card issued by the Election Commission of India, job card issued by NREGA duly signed by an officer of the State Government and letter issued by the National Population Register containing details of name and address. [KYC Master Direction, p.8]

If the OVD furnished by the customer does not have an updated address, the following documents or their equivalent e-documents shall be deemed to be OVDs for the limited purpose of proof of address:
*   Utility bill which is not more than two months old of any service provider (electricity, telephone, post-paid mobile phone, piped gas, water bill). [KYC Master Direction, p.8]
*   Property or Municipal tax receipt. [KYC Master Direction, p.8]
*   Pension or family pension payment orders (PPOs) issued to retired employees by Government Departments or Public Sector Undertakings, if they contain the address. [KYC Master Direction, p.8]
*   Letter of allotment of accommodation from employer issued by State Government or Central Government Departments, statutory or regulatory bodies, public sector undertakings. [KYC Master Direction, p.8]

question: What must a Regulated Entity obtain from an individual customer at account opening?
answer:
For undertaking Customer Due Diligence (CDD), Regulated Entities (REs) shall obtain the Aadhaar number from an individual when establishing an account-based relationship or when dealing with an individual who is a beneficial owner, authorised signatory, or power of attorney holder related to any legal entity, if:
(i) the individual desires to receive any benefit or subsidy under any scheme notified under section 7 of the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016; or
(ii) the individual decides to submit their Aadhaar number voluntarily to a bank or any RE notified under the first proviso to sub-section (1) of section 11A of the Act. [KYC Master Direction, p.24]

question: How long must REs preserve transaction records and customer identification records?
answer: REs must maintain all necessary records of transactions for at least five years from the date of transaction [KYC Master Direction, p.49]. They must preserve records pertaining to the identification of customers and their addresses for at least five years after the business relationship is ended [KYC Master Direction, p.49]. For non-profit organizations, REs must maintain registration records for a period of five years after the business relationship has ended or the account has been closed, whichever is later [KYC Master Direction, p.50].

question: How often must periodic KYC updation be done for high, medium and low risk customers?
answer: Periodic updation of KYC shall be carried out at least once in every two years for high-risk customers, once in every eight years for medium risk customers and once in every ten years for low-risk customers from the date of opening of the account / last KYC updation. [KYC Master Direction, p.39]

question: What reports must REs furnish to FIU-India, and can they freeze an account just because a report was filed?
answer:
REs must furnish information referred to in rule 3 of the PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005 to the Director, Financial Intelligence Unit- India (FIU-IND) [KYC Master Direction, p.51]. This includes Cash Transaction Reports (CTR) and Suspicious Transaction Reports (STR) [KYC Master Direction, p.51].

The provided documents do not state that REs can freeze an account just because a report was filed.

question: Is my driving licence enough as proof of identity for bank KYC?
answer: Yes, the driving licence is an "Officially Valid Document" (OVD) [KYC Master Direction, p.8].

question: If I open an account using just an OTP on my Aadhaar-linked phone, are there restrictions on it?
answer:
Yes, there are restrictions on accounts opened using Aadhaar OTP based e-KYC in non-face-to-face mode:
*   The aggregate of all credits in a financial year, across all deposit accounts, shall not exceed rupees two lakh [KYC Master Direction, p.27].
*   For borrowal accounts, only term loans can be sanctioned, and the aggregate amount of term loans sanctioned shall not exceed rupees sixty thousand in a year [KYC Master Direction, p.27].
*   Such accounts, both deposit and borrowal, are not allowed for more than one year unless identification as per paragraph 16 or paragraph 18 (V-CIP) is carried out [KYC Master Direction, p.27].
*   If the CDD procedure is not completed within a year, deposit accounts shall be closed immediately, and no further debits shall be allowed in borrowal accounts [KYC Master Direction, p.27].
*   A declaration must be obtained from the customer stating that no other account has been or will be opened using OTP based KYC in non-face-to-face mode with any other Regulated Entity (RE) [KYC Master Direction, p.27].
*   When uploading KYC information to CKYCR, REs must clearly indicate that such accounts are opened using OTP based e-KYC, and other REs shall not open accounts based on this KYC information [KYC Master Direction, p.27].

question: When a company opens a bank account, how does the bank decide who the real owner behind it is?
answer:
When a company opens a bank account, the beneficial owner is the natural person(s) who, whether acting alone or together, or through one or more juridical persons, has/have a controlling ownership interest or who exercise control through other means [KYC Master Direction, p.5].

"Controlling ownership interest" means ownership of/entitlement to more than 10 percent of the shares or capital or profits of the company [KYC Master Direction, p.5].

question: Can I give digital copies of my documents from my DigiLocker instead of physical photocopies?
answer: Yes, you can provide equivalent e-documents of Officially Valid Documents (OVDs), including documents issued through DigiLocker. [KYC Master Direction, p.30]

question: Do banks apply extra checks when a foreign public official or someone from their family opens an account?
answer:
Yes, banks do apply extra checks when a foreign public official or someone from their family opens an account.

For Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), which include individuals entrusted with prominent public functions by a foreign country, banks must:
*   Take reasonable measures to establish the source of funds/wealth [KYC Master Direction, p.46].
*   Obtain approval from senior management to open an account [KYC Master Direction, p.46].
*   Subject all such accounts to enhanced monitoring on an ongoing basis [KYC Master Direction, p.46].
*   If an existing customer or beneficial owner becomes a PEP, obtain senior management's approval to continue the business relationship [KYC Master Direction, p.46].

These instructions also apply to family members or close associates of PEPs [KYC Master Direction, p.46].

question: What are the three monetary limits on accounts opened through Aadhaar OTP-based e-KYC?
answer:
The three monetary limits on accounts opened through Aadhaar OTP-based e-KYC are:
*   The aggregate of all credits in a financial year, in all the deposit accounts taken together, shall not exceed rupees two lakh. [KYC Master Direction, p.27]
*   As regards borrowal accounts, only term loans shall be sanctioned. The aggregate amount of term loans sanctioned shall not exceed rupees sixty thousand in a year. [KYC Master Direction, p.27]
*   Accounts, both deposit and borrowal, opened using OTP based e-KYC shall not be allowed for more than one year unless identification as per paragraph 16 or as per paragraph 18 (V-CIP) is carried out. [KYC Master Direction, p.27]

question: What happens if full KYC is not completed within one year for an account opened via OTP-based e-KYC?
answer: If the CDD procedure is not completed within a year for deposit accounts opened using OTP-based e-KYC, the accounts shall be closed immediately. In the case of borrowal accounts, no further debits shall be allowed. [KYC Master Direction, p.27]

question: At what ownership percentage does someone become the beneficial owner of a company, and is the threshold the same for an unincorporated association?
answer:
For a company, "controlling ownership interest" means ownership of/entitlement to more than 10 percent of the shares or capital or profits of the company. [KYC Master Direction, p.5]

For an unincorporated association or body of individuals, the beneficial owner is the natural person(s) who has/have ownership of/entitlement to more than 15 percent of the property or capital or profits. [KYC Master Direction, p.6]

Therefore, the threshold is not the same for a company and an unincorporated association.
